extracted.intended_audience: Florida administrative agencies, regulated persons, attorneys representing parties in agency proceedings, administrative law judges, and persons substantially affected by agency action
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for filing petitions, challenging proposed or existing agency rules or unadopted statements, requesting declaratory statements, and conducting administrative hearings under Florida Chapter 120. Covers timing, burdens of proof, evidence, subpoenas, orders, and special protest procedures for procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines for challenging proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition alleging the invalidity of a proposed rule shall be filed within 21 days after the date of publication of the notice required by s. 120.54(3)(a); within 10 days after the final public hearing is held as provided by s. 120.54(3)(e)2.; within 20 days after the statement of estimated regulatory costs or revised statement has been prepared and made available as provided in s. 120.541(1)(d), if applicable; or within 20 days after the date of publication of the notice required by s. 120.54(3)(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner has the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the petitioner would be substantially affected by the proposed rule. The agency then has the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the proposed rule is not an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority as to the objections raised. A person not substantially affected by the initially noticed proposed rule, but substantially affected by a change, may challenge any provision of the resulting proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ authority and effect of invalidation of proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative law judge may declare the proposed rule wholly or partly invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the ALJ decision is reversed on appeal, the proposed rule or provision declared invalid shall not be adopted. After a petition is filed the agency may proceed with other steps in rulemaking including factfinding hearings. If part of a proposed rule is declared invalid, the agency may withdraw the proposed rule in its entirety. The agency must give notice of the decision in the first available issue of the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: No presumption of validity for challenged proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When any substantially affected person seeks the invalidity of a proposed rule the proposed rule is not presumed to be valid or invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging existing rules - timing and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition alleging the invalidity of an existing rule may be filed at any time during which the rule is in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner has the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that the existing rule is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority as to the objections raised. The ALJ may declare all or part of a rule invalid; the invalid portion becomes void when the time for filing an appeal expires, and the agency must give notice in the Florida Administrative Register in the first available issue after the rule becomes void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging agency statements defined as unadopted rules - petition content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person substantially affected by an agency statement that is an unadopted rule may seek an administrative determination that the statement violates s. 120.54(1)(a). The petition shall include the text of the statement or a description and shall state facts sufficient to show the statement constitutes an unadopted rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of proceedings when agency initiates rulemaking on challenged unadopted statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notification to the ALJ before the final hearing that the agency has published a notice of rulemaking under s. 120.54(3), such notice automatically operates as a stay of proceedings pending adoption of the statement as a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ALJ may vacate the stay for good cause shown. A stay remains in effect so long as the agency is proceeding expeditiously and in good faith to adopt the statement as a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency burden if hearing on unadopted rule held
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hearing is held and the petitioner proves the allegations of the petition, the agency shall have the burden of proving that rulemaking is not feasible or not practicable under s. 120.54(1)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ final order and publication for unadopted rule determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative law judge may determine whether all or part of a statement violates s. 120.54(1)(a). The decision of the ALJ shall constitute a final order. The division shall transmit a copy of the final order to the Department of State and the committee. The Department of State shall publish notice of the final order in the first available issue of the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency obligation to discontinue reliance after ALJ final order on unadopted rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ALJ enters a final order that all or part of an unadopted rule violates s. 120.54(1)(a), the agency must immediately discontinue all reliance upon the unadopted rule or any substantially similar statement as a basis for agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed rules addressing the challenged unadopted rule are determined to be an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority, the agency must immediately discontinue reliance until rules are properly adopted, and the ALJ shall enter a final order to that effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of proceedings involving unadopted rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings to determine a violation of s. 120.54(1)(a) shall be brought pursuant to the subsection on unadopted rules and may be consolidated with a proceeding under subsection (3) or any other section of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not prevent a party whose substantial interests have been determined by agency action from bringing a proceeding pursuant to s. 120.57(1)(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rules challenge expedited schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges to the validity of an emergency rule are subject to expedited time schedules: within 7 days after receiving the petition the division director shall assign an ALJ (if petition complies); ALJ shall conduct a hearing within 14 days unless petition is withdrawn; ALJ shall render a decision within 14 days after the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory statement petitions - who may seek and required specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any substantially affected person may seek a declaratory statement regarding an agency’s opinion as to the applicability of a statutory provision, rule, or order as it applies to the petitioner’s particular set of circumstances. The petition shall state with particularity the petitioner’s set of circumstances and shall specify the statutory provision, rule, or order believed to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency notice and deadline for declaratory statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall give notice of the filing of each petition in the next available issue of the Florida Administrative Register and transmit copies to the committee. The agency shall issue a declaratory statement or deny the petition within 90 days after filing. The declaratory statement or denial shall be noticed in the next available issue of the Florida Administrative Register. Agency disposition of petitions shall be final agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of s. 120.57 when substantial interests are determined
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of the section apply in all proceedings in which the substantial interests of a party are determined by an agency, unless proceeding under s. 120.573 or s. 120.574. Unless waived, s. 120.57(1) applies when the proceeding involves a disputed issue of material fact; s. 120.57(2) applies in all other cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a disputed issue of material fact arises during a s. 120.57(2) proceeding, it shall be terminated and a s. 120.57(1) proceeding conducted unless waived by all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content for orders affecting substantial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall be notified of any order, including a final order. Unless waived, a copy of the order shall be delivered or mailed to each party or the party’s attorney of record at the address of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each notice shall inform the recipient of any administrative hearing or judicial review available under this section, s. 120.57, or s. 120.68; indicate the procedure which must be followed to obtain the hearing or judicial review; and state the time limits which apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petitions/requests for hearing and agency referral to division
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for proceedings under s. 120.56, a petition or request for a hearing shall be filed with the agency. If the agency requests an ALJ from the division, it shall notify the division by electronic means through the division’s website within 15 days after receipt of the petition or request. A request for a hearing shall be granted or denied within 15 days after receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On request of any agency the division shall assign an ALJ with due regard to required expertise. The referring agency shall take no further action with respect to a proceeding under s. 120.57(1), except as a party litigant, while the division has jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ disqualification procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may request the disqualification of the ALJ by filing an affidavit with the division prior to taking evidence at a hearing, stating the grounds with particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum notice period for hearings involving disputed issues of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall be afforded an opportunity for a hearing after reasonable notice of not less than 14 days; the 14-day notice requirement may be waived with the consent of all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice shall include a statement of the time, place, and nature of the hearing and a statement of the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content requirements and dismissal for non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by law, a petition or request for hearing shall include those items required by the uniform rules adopted pursuant to s. 120.54(5)(b). Upon receipt the agency shall review the petition to determine if it contains all required information. A petition shall be dismissed if not in substantial compliance with requirements or if untimely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal shall, at least once, be without prejudice to filing a timely amended petition curing the defect, unless defect is incurable on its face. The agency shall promptly give written notice to all parties of action taken, state with particularity its reasons if the petition is not granted, and state the deadline for filing an amended petition if applicable. Equitable tolling remains available as a defense to untimely filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement and sanction certification
rubrics_metrics.description: All pleadings, motions, or other papers filed in the proceeding must be signed by the party, the party’s attorney, or the party’s qualified representative. The signature constitutes a certificate that the person has read the pleading, motion, or other paper and that, based upon reasonable inquiry, it is not interposed for any improper purposes (harass, cause unnecessary delay, frivolous purpose, or needless increase in litigation costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If signed in violation, the presiding officer shall impose appropriate sanctions upon the signer and/or the represented party, which may include an order to pay reasonable expenses incurred because of the filing, including reasonable attorney’s fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer has the power to swear witnesses and take their testimony under oath, to issue subpoenas, and to effect discovery on the written request of any party by any means available to the courts and in the manner provided in the Florida Rules of Civil Procedure, including imposition of sanctions, except contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No presiding officer may issue a subpoena or discovery order to a member or employee of the Legislature when it commands production of documents or testimony relating to legislative duties; such subpoenas must show on their face that the testimony sought does not relate to legislative duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of evidence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious evidence shall be excluded, but all other evidence of a type commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons in the conduct of their affairs shall be admissible, whether or not such evidence would be admissible in a Florida court trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any part of the evidence may be received in written form, and all testimony of parties and witnesses shall be under oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence and access to originals
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary evidence may be received in the form of a copy or excerpt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon request, parties shall be given an opportunity to compare the copy with the original, if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official recognition procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When official recognition of material is requested, the parties shall be notified and given an opportunity to examine and contest the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A party shall be permitted to conduct cross-examination when testimony is taken or documents are made a part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena challenge and enforcement process
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person subject to a subpoena may, before compliance and on timely petition, request the presiding officer to invalidate the subpoena on the ground that it was not lawfully issued, is unreasonably broad, or requires production of irrelevant material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may seek enforcement of a subpoena, discovery order, or sanctions order by filing a petition for enforcement in the circuit court of the judicial circuit where the noncomplying person resides. Failure to comply with court order results in contempt (except while challenging subpoena). The court may award prevailing party costs and attorney’s fees under Florida Rules of Civil Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness compensation for subpoenas
rubrics_metrics.description: Any public employee subpoenaed to appear at an agency proceeding shall be entitled to per diem and travel expenses at the same rate as state employees under s. 112.061 if travel away from headquarters is required. All other witnesses appearing pursuant to a subpoena shall be paid fees and mileage as provided in civil actions in circuit courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the case of a public employee, expenses processed and paid per agency employee travel reimbursement procedures; for non-public employees payment shall accompany the subpoena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content of final order in proceedings affecting substantial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless time is waived or extended with consent of all parties, the final order in a proceeding affecting substantial interests must be in writing and include findings of fact, if any, and conclusions of law separately stated, and it must be rendered within 90 days:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) After the hearing is concluded if conducted by the agency; 2) After a recommended order is submitted to the agency and mailed to all parties if hearing conducted by an ALJ; or 3) After the agency has received the written and oral material it authorized to be submitted if there has been no hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required substance of findings of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of fact, if set forth in a manner which is no more than mere tracking of the statutory language, must be accompanied by a concise and explicit statement of the underlying facts of record which support the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate final order for danger to public health or safety
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency head finds that an immediate danger to the public health, safety, or welfare requires an immediate final order, it shall recite with particularity the facts underlying such finding in the final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an order shall be appealable or enjoinable from the date rendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial scheduling order to manage proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of any party, the ALJ shall enter an initial scheduling order to facilitate the just, speedy, and inexpensive determination of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheduling order shall establish a discovery period (including deadline to complete discovery), the date by which parties shall identify expert witnesses and their opinions, and may require parties to meet and file a joint report by a date certain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of presentation and burdens in permit/license third-party challenges (chapters 373, 378, 403)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonapplicant petitions as a third party to challenge issuance of a license, permit, or conceptual approval, the order of presentation is: 1) permit applicant presents a prima facie case demonstrating entitlement to the license/permit/conceptual approval (may enter into evidence the application and relevant material, and agency staff report or notice of intent), followed by 2) the agency. Subsequent to applicant’s prima facie case and any direct agency evidence, the petitioner challenging issuance has the burden of ultimate persuasion and the burden of going forward to prove the case in opposition by presenting competent and substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The permit applicant and agency may on rebuttal present evidence relevant to demonstrating that the application meets conditions to approve the permit. Notwithstanding subsection (1), paragraph applies to proceedings under s. 120.574.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ assignment and use of record if replacement ALJ needed
rubrics_metrics.description: An ALJ assigned by the division shall conduct all hearings under subsection (1) (except hearings before agency heads). If assigned ALJ becomes unavailable, the division shall assign another ALJ who shall use any existing record and receive any additional evidence or argument, if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' procedural rights in hearings with disputed material facts
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall have an opportunity to respond, present evidence and argument on all issues involved, conduct cross-examination and submit rebuttal evidence, submit proposed findings of fact and orders, file exceptions to the presiding officer’s recommended order, and be represented by counsel or qualified representative. When appropriate, the public may be given an opportunity to present oral or written communications; if agency proposes to consider such material, all parties must be given opportunity to cross-examine or challenge or rebut it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearsay evidence limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearsay evidence may be used to supplement or explain other evidence, but it shall not be sufficient in itself to support a finding unless it would be admissible over objection in civil actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of similar fact evidence and notice by the state
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar fact evidence of other violations, wrongs, or acts is admissible when relevant to prove a material fact in issue (motive, opportunity, intent, preparation, identity, absence of mistake or plan, knowledge, accident), but inadmissible when relevant solely to prove bad character or propensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the state intends to offer evidence of other acts or offenses under this paragraph, it shall furnish to the affected party no fewer than 10 days before commencement of the proceeding a written statement of the acts/offenses it intends to offer, describing them and the evidence with particularity. Notice is not required for evidence used for impeachment or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on agency action based on unadopted or invalid rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency or an ALJ may not base agency action that determines the substantial interests of a party on an unadopted rule or a rule that is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not preclude application of valid adopted rules and applicable provisions of law to the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: When unadopted rules may be applied provisionally
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding prohibition, if an agency demonstrates that the statute directs it to adopt rules, that it has not had time to adopt those rules because requirement was recently enacted, that it has initiated rulemaking and is proceeding expeditiously and in good faith, then the agency’s action may be based upon those unadopted rules if the ALJ determines rulemaking is neither feasible nor practicable and the unadopted rules would not constitute an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unadopted rule shall not be presumed valid. The agency must demonstrate the unadopted rule: a) is within powers/delegated authority; b) does not enlarge/modify/contravene specific law; c) is not vague or does not vest unbridled discretion; d) is not arbitrary or capricious (arbitrary = unsupported by logic/facts; capricious = adopted without thought/reason); e) is not being applied to the substantially affected party without due notice; and f) does not impose excessive regulatory costs on the regulated person, county, or city.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record composition in cases governed by subsection (1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The record shall consist only of: all notices, pleadings, motions, and intermediate rulings; evidence admitted; matters officially recognized; proffers of proof and objections and rulings thereon; proposed findings and exceptions; any decision, opinion, order, or report by the presiding officer; all staff memoranda or data submitted to the presiding officer during the hearing or prior to disposition (after notice to all parties) except advisory staff communications permitted under s. 120.66(1); all matters placed on the record after an ex parte communication; and the official transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to preserve testimony and access to transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall accurately and completely preserve all testimony in the proceeding, and, on request of any party, it shall make a full or partial transcript available at no more than actual cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary final order when no genuine issue of material fact exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may move for a summary final order when there is no genuine issue as to any material fact. A summary final order shall be rendered if the ALJ determines from pleadings, depositions, answers to interrogatories, admissions on file, and affidavits, if any, that no genuine issue of material fact exists and the moving party is entitled as a matter of law to entry of a final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A summary final order shall consist of findings of fact, conclusions of law, disposition or penalty if applicable, and any other information required by law to be contained in the final order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment of jurisdiction when dispute of material fact no longer exists
rubrics_metrics.description: When a dispute of material fact no longer exists, any party may move the ALJ to relinquish jurisdiction to the agency. An order relinquishing jurisdiction shall be rendered if the ALJ determines from pleadings, depositions, interrogatory answers, and supporting/opposing affidavits that no genuine issue of material fact exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ALJ relinquishes jurisdiction, the agency may promptly conduct appropriate proceedings, but parties may not raise issues of disputed fact that could have been raised before the ALJ. Such an order need not contain findings of fact, conclusions of law, or a recommended disposition or penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for findings of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of fact shall be based upon a preponderance of the evidence, except in penal or licensure disciplinary proceedings or except as otherwise provided by statute, and shall be based exclusively on the evidence of record and on matters officially recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended order contents and exceptions period
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall complete and submit to the agency and all parties a recommended order consisting of findings of fact, conclusions of law, and recommended disposition or penalty if applicable, and any other information required by law in the final order. The agency shall allow each party 15 days to submit written exceptions to the recommended order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All proceedings under this subsection shall be de novo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency treatment of exceptions to recommended order
rubrics_metrics.description: The final order shall include an explicit ruling on each exception, but an agency need not rule on an exception that does not clearly identify the disputed portion of the recommended order by page number or paragraph, that does not identify the legal basis for the exception, or that does not include appropriate and specific citations to the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency may adopt, reject, or modify recommended orders with required particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may adopt the recommended order as the final order. The agency may reject or modify conclusions of law over which it has substantive jurisdiction and interpretation of administrative rules over which it has substantive jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rejecting or modifying such conclusions or interpretations, the agency must state with particularity its reasons and must make a finding that its substituted conclusion or interpretation is as or more reasonable than that rejected or modified. Rejection/modification of conclusions of law may not be the basis to reject/modify findings of fact. The agency may accept a recommended penalty but may not change it without review of the complete record and stating with particularity its reasons in the order, citing the record in justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to provide final order and exceptions to division
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recommended order is submitted to an agency, the agency shall provide a copy of its final order and any exceptions to the division within 15 days after the order is filed with the agency clerk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority to resolve conflicting statutory time requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, when statutes or rules impose conflicting time requirements for scheduling expedited hearings or issuance of recommended or final orders, the director of the division shall have the authority to set the proceedings for orderly operation of the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duties in non-disputed hearings (subsection (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case not involving disputed issues of material fact, the agency shall: 1) Give reasonable notice to affected persons of the action of the agency (proposed or already taken or refusal to act), together with a summary of the factual, legal, and policy grounds for the action; and 2) Give parties or counsel the option to present written or oral evidence in opposition or a written statement challenging the agency’s grounds. If objections are overruled, provide a written explanation within 7 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record composition in non-disputed cases
rubrics_metrics.description: For hearings not involving disputed issues of material fact, the record shall consist of: the notice and summary of grounds; evidence received; all written statements submitted; any decision overruling objections; all matters placed on the record after an ex parte communication; the official transcript; and any decision/opinion/order/report by the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract solicitation/award protest electronic notice and mandatory waiver statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall provide notice of a decision or intended decision concerning a solicitation, contract award, or exceptional purchase by electronic posting. This notice shall contain the statement: 'Failure to file a protest within the time prescribed in section 120.57(3), Florida Statutes, or failure to post the bond or other security required by law within the time allowed for filing a bond shall constitute a waiver of proceedings under chapter 120, Florida Statutes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing notices of protest and formal written protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person adversely affected by the agency decision or intended decision shall file with the agency a notice of protest in writing within 72 hours after the posting of the notice of decision or intended decision. The formal written protest shall be filed within 10 days after the date the notice of protest is filed. With respect to protest of terms/conditions/specifications in a solicitation, notice of protest shall be filed in writing within 72 hours after posting of the solicitation. Saturdays, Sundays, and state holidays are excluded in computation of the 72-hour periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal written protest shall state with particularity the facts and law upon which the protest is based. Failure to file the notice of protest or formal written protest constitutes waiver of proceedings under chapter 120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency stay of solicitation/award upon timely formal written protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a timely formal written protest, the agency shall stop the solicitation or contract award process until the subject of the protest is resolved by final agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is excepted if the agency head sets forth in writing particular facts and circumstances requiring continuance of the solicitation/award process without delay to avoid an immediate and serious danger to public health, safety, or welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to resolve protest by mutual agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall provide an opportunity to resolve the protest by mutual agreement between the parties within 7 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and state holidays, after receipt of a formal written protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding pathways after unsuccessful protest settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subject of a protest is not resolved by mutual agreement within 7 days and there is no disputed issue of material fact, an informal proceeding shall be conducted pursuant to subsection (2) and applicable agency rules before a person whose qualifications are prescribed by agency rules. If unresolved and there is a disputed issue of material fact, the agency shall refer the protest to the division for proceedings under subsection (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division timelines for assigned procurement protest hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a formal written protest referred to the division, the director shall expedite the hearing and assign an ALJ who shall commence a hearing within 30 days after receipt of the formal written protest by the division and enter a recommended order within 30 days after the hearing or within 30 days after receipt of the hearing transcript by the ALJ, whichever is later. Each party has 10 days to submit written exceptions to the recommended order. A final order shall be entered by the agency within 30 days of the entry of a recommended order. These timelines may be waived upon stipulation by all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest evidentiary limitations relating to post-opening submissions and burden/standards of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: In a protest to an invitation to bid or request for proposals, no submissions made after the bid or proposal opening which amend or supplement the bid or proposal shall be considered. In a protest to an invitation to negotiate, no submissions made after the agency announces its intent to award, reject all replies, or withdraw the solicitation which amend or supplement the reply shall be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise provided by statute, the burden of proof rests with the protesting party. In a competitive-procurement protest (other than rejection of all bids/proposals/replies), the ALJ shall conduct a de novo proceeding to determine whether the agency’s proposed action is contrary to the agency’s governing statutes, rules or policies, or solicitation specifications. Standard of proof: whether the proposed agency action was clearly erroneous, contrary to competition, arbitrary, or capricious. In any bid-protest contesting intended agency action to reject all bids/proposals/replies, standard is whether agency’s intended action is illegal, arbitrary, dishonest, or fraudulent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for procurement protests
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of procurement protest subsection, the definitions in s. 287.012 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal disposition allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precluded by law, informal disposition may be made of any proceeding by stipulation, agreed settlement, or consent order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section inapplicability to preliminary agency investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: This section (120.57) does not apply to agency investigations preliminary to agency action.
